summary: The note covers an International Cybersecurity Consortium (ICC) review of National Cybersecurity Strategies (NCS) launched on September 15, 2023, in which over 120 countries took part. It highlights success stories from Norway, Singapore and Canada and key themes: agility against evolving threats, cyber education, public-private partnerships, AI adoption, and international treaties. It concludes that nations are building a stronger, more collaborative digital safety net.
one_line: The ICC's review of national cybersecurity strategies, begun in 2023, highlights agility, education, public-private partnerships, AI and international treaties as keys to cyber resilience.
key_facts: The International Cybersecurity Consortium (ICC) launched a comprehensive review of National Cybersecurity Strategies on September 15, 2023.
Dr. Elizabeth Moreno, an internationally renowned cybersecurity expert, conceptualized the review initiative.
Over 120 countries volunteered their NCS for scrutiny and mutual learning.
The strategies of Norway, Singapore, and Canada were applauded for forward-looking approaches and comprehensive scope.
General Paul Anderson led the ICC's assessment team and praised the camaraderie and collaboration among nations.
Norway's Cybersecurity Council, established in late 2023, coordinates national cyber defenses and fosters public-private partnerships.
Singapore's Cybersecurity Agency (CSA) set the gold standard with its Cybersecurity Strategy 2025, focused on a resilient digital ecosystem and a skilled cybersecurity workforce.
Canada's multi-layered strategy covers critical infrastructure protection, cyber crime legislation, and international collaboration.
At a webinar on February 20, 2024, Dr. Moreno said some strategies failed to account for the agility of cyber threats: "Flexibility and evolution are key."

The global 'CyberSmart' initiative, launched in March 2024, integrates cybersecurity awareness into educational curriculums and lifelong learning platforms, funded by participating nations and private partners.
The Cybersecurity Tech Accord is an agreement among global tech companies to protect civilians online and improve the security, stability, and resilience of cyberspace.
At the AI Cyber Summit on June 12, 2024, nations shared insights on integrating AI-driven threat intelligence, with consensus that AI is a necessary ally.
The Cybersecurity Protocol Treaty, signed by 80 nations in August 2024, provides guidelines for information sharing, cybercrime jurisdiction, and coordinated responses to cross-border incidents.
